reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in aligning inertial motion capture data with external positioning systems—specifically, resolving discrepancies in reference frames caused by magnetic field distortions and ambiguous marker-to-sensor associations. Inertial systems inherently drift over time, necessitating periodic correction from external aids. However, these corrections fail when the magnetic field is inhomogeneous, rendering compass-based heading unreliable. Additionally, passive optical markers cannot self-identify, leading to combinatorial ambiguity in associating them with respective sensing units. These issues compound into a dual failure mode: one rooted in physical environmental constraints (magnetic distortion), and another in data interpretation (marker association). The solution must therefore incorporate robust statistical inference mechanisms to mitigate both types of errors through probabilistic alignment and constrained optimization of sensor-marker pairings.
